lines.line: His own math: 1,000 bots, $1.2 million a year.
lines.emotion: Indignant disbelief at easy money from cheating (a million a year, from bots?), then the itch of whose money that is: everyone knows bots aren't listeners, so a paycheck for fake listening feels like it must come out of a real person's pocket, and one man's own numbers make it concrete and believable.
lines.backing: FL 4.12 (DOJ, primary: Smith's own estimate of 1,040 bot accounts, ~661,440 plays a day, $1,207,128 a year; the FL's safe wording is "His own math"); FL 4.10 + 7.10 (his songs came from an unnamed AI music tool; 2017-2024 on four services; $14M+ received in total); FL 4.9 (18 months); FL 3.1-3.3 (a shared pot per country per month, split by share of plays); FL 4.1-4.2 (caught fakes earn nothing); FL 4.14-4.15 + 8.6 (harm contested: air the defence and Spotify's ~$60,000; never "$8M stolen from artists"); FL 8.1-8.2 (no measured loss; slip-through unknown). The AI songs come in line 2, by ~3 s.
lines.payoff: His million a year came out of the same shared pot that pays every real artist, split by share of plays, so every bot play that slipped past the filters took a slice; he got 18 months, the apps now strip out the fakes they catch, and the ones that still slip through thin every real slice by an amount nobody has measured.

lines.line: He used bots instead of listeners, and got 18 months.
lines.emotion: Shock plus a 'wait, why?' itch: having bots play your own songs sounds harmless, almost funny, so 18 months in prison makes a normal viewer ask who on earth got hurt, and that question carries the whole video to the pot.
lines.backing: FL 4.9 + 1.8 (18 months, SDNY, 2026-10-06; the FL's safe wording: "for having bots play his AI songs"); FL 6.3 (the U.S. Attorney's own phrase, "automated bots in the place of consumers"); FL 4.10 + 7.10 (hundreds of thousands of AI songs from an unnamed tool, billions of plays per prosecutors, four services, 2017-2024); FL 3.1-3.3 + 3.7 (shared pot; more plays in it, smaller shares); FL 4.1-4.2 (caught fakes stripped out); FL 4.14-4.15 (harm contested: air both sides); FL 8.1-8.2.
lines.payoff: It's a crime because streaming pays from a shared pot split by share of plays, so his bots' plays took a slice from every real artist in those pots until he was stopped, which is why the apps now strip out every fake play they catch, and why the ones they miss still matter.

lines.line: A prosecutor says his bots robbed real artists, and their fans.
lines.frame0: PROSECUTOR: HIS BOTS "ROBBED" ARTISTS AND FANS
lines.emotion: Outrage at theft, then the twist: 'and their fans' means people like the viewer, so 'how could bots rob me?' becomes the question the video answers; an official's own words make it feel serious, not like internet outrage.
lines.backing: FL 6.3 (verbatim: "Smith robbed millions in royalty payments from genuine artists and their fans"; card 'Jamie McDonald, U.S. Attorney, Oct 2026', with the full sentence or a marked cut); FL 4.14-4.15 (contested: the defence says no artist "suffered any appreciable loss", and Spotify says it held his Spotify take to ~$60,000: both must air, and 'says' stays on frame 0 like v2's SHE SAYS); FL 3.3 + 3.11 (fans' fees fill the shared pot, not just their own artists' share); FL 4.9-4.10; FL 8.1 + 8.6 (never "$8M stolen from artists", no per-artist sum).
lines.payoff: Fans' fees fill a shared pot split by share of plays, so every bot play that slipped past the filters took a sliver from every real artist in it; his lawyers say no artist suffered "any appreciable loss", and both can be true: a thin slice off everyone, by an amount nobody has measured.

lines.line: A fan congratulated her on an album she never made.
lines.frame0: HER NEW ALBUM? SHE NEVER MADE IT.
lines.emotion: A small chill of violation plus 'could I tell?': the question everyone asks about AI songs, put in one real fan's mouth; anyone with a favorite singer pictures it happening to them.
lines.backing: FL 6.7 (folk singer Emily Portman, AFP, VERIFIED: an AI album went live under her name; impersonation only, no money loss implied; keep AFP's ellipsis on her quote; ask before drawing her); FL 5.1 + 8.7 ("In a blind test, 97% of 9,000 people couldn't tell"); FL 2.1-2.5 (one app: over half of new uploads on peak days, 1-3% of plays, up to 85% of those fake in 2025, fake plays the main purpose per Deezer); FL 3.1-3.3; FL 4.1-4.2; FL 8.1-8.2. Risk (FL 5.14): the pot can't pay off impersonation, so the turn must say plainly that the fakes touching every artist's pay need no fans, only bots.
lines.payoff: You don't have to be fooled for fakes to cost real artists: bots do the playing, and the shared pot, split by share of plays, pays out for every fake play the filters miss, a thin slice off every real artist, by an amount nobody has measured.

lines.line: His trick: a TON of AI songs, a few bot plays each.
lines.frame0: TONS OF AI SONGS, FEW PLAYS EACH
lines.emotion: The thrill of seeing a con from the inside: a fraudster's own plan, simple and sneaky, lets the viewer in on a secret, then makes them wonder who paid for all those little plays.
lines.backing: FL 4.11 (his Oct 2018 email in the court record, verbatim: "in order to not raise any issues with the powers that be we need a TON of content with small amounts of Streams"; card 'Michael Smith, email, 2018 (court papers)'); FL 4.10 + 7.10 (the content was AI songs from an unnamed tool, played by bot accounts billions of times per prosecutors); FL 2.5 (Deezer: fake plays are the main reason AI songs get uploaded, one app); FL 2.8-2.9 (cheap to make and upload); FL 3.1-3.3; FL 3.9-3.10 (Spotify now pays nothing below 1,000 plays a year); FL 4.1-4.2; FL 8.2.
lines.payoff: A few plays each, times a TON of songs, came to billions of plays, prosecutors say, and every one that got past the filters took a slice of the same shared pot real artists are paid from; AI now makes the TON almost free, which is why the filters that strip fakes out of the pot matter so much.

lines.line: Apple Music's boss on fake plays: "This is a zero-sum game."
lines.frame0: FAKE PLAYS: "THIS IS A ZERO-SUM GAME"
lines.emotion: Curiosity with a sting: most people assume a fake play costs nobody, and 'zero-sum' from the man who runs Apple Music means somebody real always pays; an insider's own words, with no villain.
lines.backing: FL 6.4 (verbatim, said while raising fraud penalties; card 'Oliver Schusser, Apple Music, on streaming fraud, Jan 2026'; he is the Apple VP who runs Apple Music); FL 3.1-3.3 (each market's pot is set by its revenue and split by share of plays); FL 3.7 (Spotify: "as total streams grow, you need more streams to maintain the same share"); FL 3.13 (Apple puts caught-fraud money back in the pool, REPORTED); FL 4.1-4.2 + 4.4 (caught fakes stripped); FL 8.1-8.2.
lines.payoff: Each month's pot is set by what subscribers and ads paid in and split by share of plays, so a fake play the filters miss is paid for by every real artist in that pot, a sliver each, while the money from fakes Apple catches goes back into the pool "so that it goes to honorable artists."

lines.emotion: Uncanny unease, like reading the DM yourself: her fans sensed something off about a song on her page, which is the 'can I even tell?' fuss in one real message (and it gives the first second a natural message ding).
lines.backing: FL 6.6 (indie-folk singer Ormella to TIME, REPORTED, one outlet: "I had a lot of fans message me, asking, 'Is it you? It doesn't sound like you,'"; an AI song on her profile; impersonation, and she claims no money loss; card 'Ormella, singer, to TIME, March 2026'; ask before drawing her); FL 5.1 + 8.7; FL 2.3-2.5; FL 3.1-3.3; FL 4.1-4.2; FL 8.2. Risk (FL 5.14): the turn must leave impersonation for fake plays.
lines.payoff: Fans ask 'is it you?' and bots never do: fake accounts play their own songs on repeat, and the shared pot counts every play the filters miss, so every real artist's slice gets a little thinner, by an amount nobody has measured.

lines.line: If AI slop pads the plays, your favorite artist's share shrinks.
lines.frame0: SLOP PADDING PLAYS? YOUR ARTIST GETS LESS.
lines.emotion: Protective worry for the artist you love: songs you'd never play can still shrink their share, which feels unfair because you never chose them, and it answers 'I don't listen to that stuff, so who cares?'
lines.backing: FL 6.1 (Morgan Hayduk, NBC 2026-10-20, verbatim: "If the denominator has grown because of AI slop, the percentage that each legitimate rights holder or artist will receive is diminished"; his firm Beatdapp sells fraud detection, so the card and the voice say so; the logic only, never a size); FL 3.2 + 3.7 (Spotify concedes the denominator effect); FL 2.3-2.4 (on one app, AI tracks' few plays were mostly fake in 2025); FL 4.1-4.2 (caught fakes don't count); FL 3.9-3.10 (most AI tracks never reach Spotify's pay line); FL 8.1. Risk: his words blame 'AI slop', so the script narrows it to fake plays that slip through (fraud, not AI).
lines.payoff: Streaming splits each month's pot by share of all plays, so every fake play that slips past the filters grows the total and shrinks every real share, your favorite artist's included, by an amount nobody has measured, which is why caught fakes get stripped out before anyone is paid.
